implementation_notes: Rust already removes most of the enum-shaped scatter: a `match` on a `#[non_exhaustive]`-free enum is checked for exhaustiveness, so adding a variant is a compile error at every site. The remaining scatter is structural — a struct field added to a type that is constructed in many places, and traits implemented by many types when you add a method. The idiom is to put the field behind a constructor that takes the whole struct (so construction sites use `..Default::default()`), and to prefer data-carrying enums over a tag field plus a match. `Default` plus struct update syntax is the practical single-site construction idiom.
idiom_name: adding a variant to an enum handled in many match sites
pitfalls: Adding a method to a widely implemented trait is shotgun surgery across every impl — prefer a free function or a defaulted trait method.
Adding an enum variant without `#[non_exhaustive]` breaks every downstream match, which is loud (good) but can be suppressed by a wildcard arm.
`serde` renames turn a field rename into a wire-format change in every serialiser.
